messages:
maya: FYI nightly perf job shows a spike in GPU memory during multi-GPU TP32 runs, looks like ~11-13GB extra per worker compared to baseline. repro steps attached.
alex: can you drop the nvidia-smi snapshot and the exact model/shard config?
maya: sure, running on 8xA40 TP=8 seq=2048 batch=1, model=redwood-13b-ptq. nvidia-smi snippet: ```+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+| GPU Memory-Usage | | 0  11264MiB / 49664MiB | 1  11270MiB / 49664MiB | ...```
samir: that magnitude smells like duplicated NCCL comm buffers + staging workspace. Did the run enable kvcache-prefetch and large batching heuristic?
maya: yes, kvcache-prefetch=true, batching policy auto with short-buffer warmup. Turning prefetch off drops the extra ~10GB.
jamie: interesting — maybe when KV cache gets prefetched across TP shards we allocate per-rank staging buffers for each shard and for each kernel selection path. Kernel selector may pick a larger workspace for fused attention when sequence distribution looks skewed.
alex: do we have a profiler trace for the run (nvtx/heap) that shows allocator peaks vs NCCL allocs?
maya: uploaded perf flame to the run: looks like peaks coincide with "ncclCommInitRank" and a repeated call in the staging path. heap profile shows many small cudaMallocs around comm setup.
ci-bot: perf-regression-detector detected 24% memory increase vs last stable for the same config, tagging @eng-runtime.
samir: hypothesis: comm buffers are being lazily allocated per-stream per-shard instead of using a shared comm pool. Combined with kvcache prefetch (which pins fragments in workspace) this pushes the allocator to create separate temporary slabs.
jamie: I'd try two quick changes: 1) enable a small pre-reserved shared NCCL comm pool (one buffer per-device reused across TP shards) and 2) clamp kernel workspace selection when KV prefetch is active (reduce heuristic multiplier).
maya: patched local branch to reuse comm-buffer pool + lowered workspace multiplier from 1.5->1.1, quick run shows peak drops by ~9.5GB and zero OOMs.
alex: nice. any regression on latency or throughput?
maya: negligible latency hit (~1.8% p50 increase) but steady throughputs unchanged for batch=1. Need wider perf matrix.
samir: ok create a microbenchmark: matrix across seq lengths [512,1024,2048], tp [2,4,8], kvcache on/off, compare memory, p50, p95. Also include kernel-selection logs to ensure we're not forcing slower kernels.
jamie: also add a test that simulates spill-to-disk/eviction path so we can see allocator behavior when kvcache pages churn.
alex: sounds good. maya can you open a PR with the pool+clamp, attach perf results and rollout plan (gradual rollout + canary on dedicated infra)?
maya: on it. PR in a few hours, will include repro script and perf CSVs. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: smoke tests queued for the branch.
